weak_acceptance_criteria.description: The acceptance criteria for US-002 does not specify how the system validates the payment status update or what actions are taken upon successful processing beyond updating the internal state. This lacks sufficient detail to ensure testability and completeness.
weak_acceptance_criteria.recommended_action: Enhance the acceptance criteria to explicitly define the validation logic and the specific outcome (e.g., state update, error handling) when a callback is processed successfully.

weak_acceptance_criteria.description: The acceptance criteria for US-007 does not specify which actors are authorized to trigger state transitions or how the actor is determined (e.g., webhook, customer, support agent). This introduces ambiguity in testability and operational clarity.
weak_acceptance_criteria.recommended_action: Clarify the acceptance criteria to explicitly define the actors that can trigger state transitions and how the actor identity is captured in the audit log.

weak_acceptance_criteria.description: The acceptance criteria for US-008 does not specify the content or structure of the email notification, which is required by REQ-011. This makes it impossible to verify compliance with the requirement.
weak_acceptance_criteria.recommended_action: Add a detailed specification of the email content, including subject line, body, and fields such as refund amount, order ID, and status, to ensure testability and alignment with REQ-011.

traceability_gaps.description: US-009 is not linked to any requirement in the plan, creating a traceability gap for the monitoring dashboard implementation. This undermines accountability and compliance verification.
traceability_gaps.recommended_action: Link US-009 to REQ-031, which recommends implementing a monitoring dashboard for webhook delivery metrics, to ensure full traceability and alignment with functional requirements.
